rejected.title: Hormones in pregnancy
card: Hormones are chemical messengers carried in the blood. In pregnancy they keep the body in a state that supports the embryo and then the fetus.
Progesterone
keeps the lining of the uterus thick and rich in blood vessels, so the embryo can stay implanted. It also helps stop the uterus contracting during pregnancy.
Oestrogen
also helps maintain the uterus lining and supports the growth of the uterus. Its level rises as pregnancy continues.
At first the ovary makes these hormones. After implantation, the placenta also makes them, and later it makes most of them. This keeps their levels high without the normal monthly cycle.
rejected.remember: Progesterone and oestrogen keep the uterus lining in place, and the placenta also makes them.

a.q: Why are high levels of progesterone needed during early pregnancy?
opts: They keep the uterus lining thick so the embryo stays put
They make an egg release from the ovary each month
They make the uterus lining break down and leave the body
They carry oxygen from the mother to the embryo
a.why: Progesterone keeps the uterus lining thick and rich in blood vessels, which supports the implanted embryo. If the lining broke down, as in a normal monthly cycle, the embryo would be lost.
a.clue: Think about what the embryo is attached to.

b.q: Mei is 20 weeks pregnant. Her ovaries are making much less hormone than before, yet her progesterone level stays high. What best explains this?
opts: The placenta is making progesterone
The embryo has stopped needing any hormones
The uterus lining is being shed each month
The ovaries have started releasing a new egg
b.why: After implantation the placenta also makes progesterone and oestrogen, so levels stay high even when the ovaries make less. Hormones are still needed to support the pregnancy, and a monthly shedding of the lining would end it.
b.clue: Which organ forms during pregnancy and can also make hormones?

draft.title: Hormones in pregnancy
card: Hormones are chemical messengers carried in the blood. In pregnancy, some of them keep the body able to support the developing baby.
Progesterone
keeps the lining of the uterus thick and rich in blood vessels, so the embryo stays in place. It also helps stop the uterus contracting.
Oestrogen
also helps maintain the uterus lining and supports the growth of the uterus.
Placenta
At first the ovary makes these hormones. The placenta, an organ that forms in pregnancy, then also makes them, and later makes most of them.
draft.remember: Progesterone and oestrogen support the pregnancy, and the placenta becomes a main source of them.

a.q: Progesterone drops sharply in early pregnancy. What is the most likely effect?
opts: The lining could thin and the pregnancy could be lost
The lining would get thicker to protect the embryo
The uterus would contract less often than before
The embryo would make progesterone instead
a.why: Progesterone keeps the uterus lining thick, so a sharp drop could let the lining thin and the pregnancy be lost. Contractions would not lessen, because progesterone helps stop the uterus contracting.
a.clue: Think about what progesterone does to the uterus lining.

b.q: Why can hormone levels stay high in late pregnancy, when the ovary is no longer the main source?
opts: The placenta now makes most of the hormones
The uterus wall itself makes them as it stretches
The fetus makes them and passes them to the mother
The ovary makes more of them as the fetus grows
b.why: The placenta also makes progesterone and oestrogen, and later makes most of them. The ovary is the early source, so it is not the reason levels stay high later.
b.clue: Which organ forms during pregnancy and makes hormones?

a.best: The lining could thin and the pregnancy could be lost

b.best: The placenta now makes most of the hormones
